title: Sponsor signature bypass in inner batch transactions allows unauthorized reserve locking
key_points: Inner batch transactions can include an empty sfSponsorSignature object, bypassing sponsorship checks.
For non-batch transactions, sponsor signatures are verified later but this is skipped for inner batch transactions.
This allows an attacker to specify any account as a reserve sponsor without that account's consent.
The root cause is in the checkSponsor function which incorrectly assumes the signature will be validated later by checkSign for inner batch transactions.
Either fixing Batch::preflightSigValidated or Batch::preflight would prevent this exploit
limitations: Depends on the exact fixes chosen
The suggested fix requires careful review to ensure it won't break other functionality
Potentially impacts performance and complexity of inner batch processing logic
asserts: Inner batch transactions can be exploited to bypass sponsorship checks and lock arbitrary amounts of any account's reserves without authorization.
scope: This exploit applies to the current implementation of XRPL's inner batch transaction sponsorship checks and could be used by an attacker to fraudulently increase other accounts' required reserves.
